throughput.note: "delivered" counts every work_item_closed event (351 closes vs 126 recorded metric rides) — this includes administrative and non-feature doc closes, not only full agent rides

speed.note: busy_seconds is summed agent duration (agent busy time), NOT calendar wall-clock

cost.usd_note: no USD figure is derivable — tokens_in/out are null across the ledger and the usage marker is an undecomposed total with no in/out split to price

quality.review_verdict_note: per-review pass/fail lives only in prose run notes and is not mechanically derived; only ride verdict + code_review_completed count are shown

items.what: Codex P1 on PR #242 (enforce flip): under usage_capture_gate: enforce there is no per-run CLI correction for a run whose usage marker was omitted — append-run only appends, STATE hand-edits are forbidden, so the supported recovery today is the dial toggle (report-only -> close -> enforce) plus the usage_capture=none sentinel for honest gaps.
orchestrator must never git add -A while a subagent edits the same worktree; stage explicit paths
orchestrator must verify git show --stat after every commit, not the exit code
decide explicitly whether the remaining shell twin surface (sh plus ps1) is a standing cost we accept or a port we schedule
the specimen mask's pipe-preservation clause is not mutation-pinned: removing it from maskCodeSpecimens survives the whole spec-lint suite
the specimen masker in spec-lint.mjs duplicates docs-audit-core.mjs:782-875 more weakly, reintroducing both bugs that file fixed under SPEC-0013 W3
ac-vague-term reports the Test Plan row's line number when the Test Plan section precedes the AC table (measured 19 vs 25)
CHANGE-0144's TEST-011(clarify) allowlists .aai/ paths against the BRANCH diff, so every future scope that touches .aai/ must edit that test or go red
the allocator's completion line hardcodes docs/INDEX.md into the regenerated list, so it names the file even when generate-docs-index.mjs is absent and nothing was rewritten
the spec's edge case says the rollup generator no-ops when USER_GUIDE.md is absent; it CREATES the file
regenerateIndex() swallows generator failures with no named stderr line, unlike the two spec-page generators
the universal no-regeneration arm never exercises a --reserve that actually allocates
orchestration-dispatch matched rule 6 and dispatched Planning onto a scope it already knew was closed
set-focus to a new ref leaves the previous scope's spec_path in current_focus, so the next dispatch hands the role a foreign spec as an input
SUBAGENT_CONTRACT forbids subagent STATE writes while the dispatch block explicitly directs them; two roles hit it independently in one ride
the TDD role declares done after targeted suites only, so defects visible only to the full framework sweep surface two roles later and cost a whole validate-remediate lap each
a validation pass survives a later remediation that rewrites the validated code, and the default routing skips re-validation
a validator probe helper ran git commands against the real repository and created two commits on main
TEST-020 corpus regex is thin though it does bite
my role dispatches pre-rank findings and name the pattern to look for, which frames the answer before the role forms one

state-engine.mjs nowIso() truncates ISO timestamps to the second while append-event.mjs keeps milliseconds; orchestration-dispatch.mjs now defends against this at the comparison site (Date.parse + Number.isFinite instants), but the two producers still disagree at the source
TEST-020's corpus scan is polarity-blind and passes only by accident
writing about a control-character escape reliably inserts the control character itself into the prose
nothing checks tracked text files for NUL bytes, so a control character can silently turn a source file binary to POSIX grep
validation picks its suites from the declared review scope while CI picks them from select-suites, so a CORE suite can be skipped in validation and fail in CI
after pushing a PR the orchestrator stops instead of watching CI, so a failure sits undetected until the owner asks

generate-factory-report.mjs:616 publishes follow_ups.open_count: 0 for an UNREADABLE ledger (e.g. --decisions a directory), the same 'a bad input reads as good news' shape D2 refuses on the CLI; the file's own oldest_age_days convention two lines down already uses null, never 0, for exactly this degradation
file_content_different in aai-sync.sh treats an unobtainable hash as different, so a transient sha256sum hiccup silently rewrites the target's copilot shim and plants a project-overrides file
No guard stops a NEW test or script from pinning a bare 'main' ref that silently never resolves on a pull_request checkout

No mechanical guard remains that a pre-existing arm or assertion in tests/skills/test-aai-deslop.sh is not removed: TEST-027 (test_027_suite_stays_green_and_additive) was mechanized four times, failed independent validation four times, and was withdrawn 2026-08-18, taking the suite-additivity clause of Spec-AC-06 with it.

The PR ceremony ordering - run close-work-item.mjs BEFORE the push, not after - is currently only a habit; nothing enforces it, so a ride can push first and then spend a round chasing framework reds that the close would have cleared.
TEST-005 (no-write proof) never asserts the engine's exit code, so an engine that dies before doing anything passes it vacuously
SPEC-0132 says its no-write and corpus arms compare manifests with cmp, but tests/skills/test-aai-deslop.sh invokes no cmp command - the comparisons are shell string compares
TEST-023's real-tree citation loop depends on a single non-docs/specs citation per symbol (CHANGE-0125 twice, CHANGE-0096 once)
TEST-028 asserts docs-audit is clean by checking its EXIT CODE, but docs-audit exits 0 even at NEEDS-TRIAGE, so the arm is green while the audit is not clean
log_fail in tests/skills/test-aai-doc-numbering.sh calls exit 1, so the first failed assertion aborts the whole suite and every later arm silently never runs
mutation testing has no rig, so each trial rsyncs the whole 119 MB tree and re-runs a full suite; nine trials plus a fixture battery cost one validation round five and a half hours
validation round 7 returned a full verdict in its subagent record but never wrote its report to docs/ai/validation, so the on-disk evidence trail jumps round6 to round8
TEST-026's d3 draft-only fixture body says --draft-only-flag must still be reported, but no assertion in that arm checks the flag is reported
no suite arm fails on the --diff balance clause alone: both --diff balance assertions sit beside literal pins on the same two numbers
the four ln -s dangling-symlink fixtures in tests/skills/test-aai-deslop.sh are unverified on Windows and Git-Bash
seven report-line assertions in tests/skills/test-aai-deslop.sh remain unanchored grep -qF substring probes after R-15 and R-20 anchored the corpus/bucket headers
close-work-item.mjs requires --pr <N>, but the correct ceremony order runs it BEFORE the push that creates the PR, so the number must be guessed
collectSurfaceFiles calls walk() without the unreadableDirs collector, so an unreadable directory under .aai/scripts is still silently skipped
the repo tripwire compares git status --porcelain=v1, which reports a path's change CLASS not its content, so a second write to an already-dirty path is invisible
docs/ai/tests/test-runs.jsonl is tracked AND listed in .gitignore, so tests/skills/test-framework.sh dirties the working tree on every run
tests/skills/test-aai-hitl-propagation.sh regenerates docs/INDEX.md in PROJECT_ROOT, leaving the tracked file modified after every run
tests/skills/test-aai-metrics.sh rewrites docs/ai/overview.html and docs/ai/overview-data.json in PROJECT_ROOT

AC STATUS GATE rule 1 blocks PASS on non-terminal AC rows while docs-audit's false-open heuristic fails closed on a terminal AC table with un-timestampable delivery, stripping the CLEAN token and turning TEST-013 red
the tripwire is silently defeatable by git plumbing: update-index --assume-unchanged then write, or appending a pattern to the untracked .git/info/exclude then creating files under it
tests/skills/test-aai-state.sh rewrites the tracked docs/INDEX.md in PROJECT_ROOT on every run
tests/skills/test-aai-token-capture.sh rewrites the tracked docs/ai/overview.html and docs/ai/overview-data.json in PROJECT_ROOT on every run
follow-ups.mjs list --json stops at exactly 65536 bytes when stdout is a pipe, emitting invalid JSON, while the same command redirected to a file completes

tripwire_path_listed loops over an unquoted $2, so a ratchet path list undergoes word-splitting and pathname expansion; an entry reading docs/* covers whatever the glob matches in the framework's CWD at run time
tripwire_allowlist_entry returns on the first match, so a second ratchet entry naming the same suite is dead code and nothing warns that the two collide
the suite-map row for aai-repo-tripwire omits tests/skills/test-aai-spec-lint.sh and .aai/system/PROFILES.yaml, both of which this scope changed and the suite depends on
a suite that fails on its OWN exit code AND trips the tripwire prints only the tripwire block, so the failure-lines-plus-tail dump that makes a CI log diagnosable is lost
writes to .git internals (git config --local, hooks, refs, the stash, reflog) are invisible to the tripwire and are not named as a limit beside D3 and D7
the mktemp snapshot files .aai/scripts/aai-run-tests.sh creates for the tripwire leak on a signal because the script installs no trap to remove them
dispatching a code review and a validation concurrently makes the review's own report file land in the checkout mid-run, which the tripwire correctly reports as a suite dirtying the shipping repo
the ratchet entry path-subset test compares only paths that MOVED, so an allowlisted suite writing an already-dirty non-ratchet path still reads tripwire ALLOWED inside its listed paths at exit 0
under the no-hasher degrade a masked writer's own progress line is a bare PASS and metrics.jsonl records tripwire clean with tripwire_attested true; only the two aggregate WARN lines are honest
validation reports list follow-up ids under a 'filed:' key when the role only SUGGESTED them, so the orchestrator relays them as filed and they never enter the ledger
the vendor-facing CONTRACT block in repo-tripwire.sh omits aai_tripwire_hash_usable and aai_tripwire_hasher and states no hash-side limit
the clean-to-dirty escalation lifts only the 'clean' state, so hash evidence is discarded when tw_state is 'unavailable', and the lost-snapshot block names no paths

tests/skills/test-framework.sh derives RUN_DIR from a second-resolution RUN_ID, so two framework processes started in the same second share one results dir and overwrite each other's per-suite tripwire snapshots
tests/skills/test-aai-repo-tripwire.sh new_fixture is always called in a command substitution, so its WORKDIRS+= runs in a subshell and the EXIT trap sees an empty array

test-aai-docs-audit.sh TEST-003 regenerates docs/INDEX.md and diffs it against the committed one, so it is RED for the whole life of any scope that adds a doc, and test-aai-delta-stage3.sh TEST-007 inherits the failure

every .mjs CLI guards main() with path.resolve(process.argv[1]) === fileURLToPath(import.meta.url), which is FALSE whenever the checkout is reached through a symlink, so the CLI exits 0 having printed nothing

the three-step working-tree seeding (tracked diff replay, untracked-not-ignored copy, gitignored per-dev seed) is implemented twice, once in tests/skills/test-framework.sh and once in .aai/scripts/aai-run-tests.sh

the orchestrator's liveness check for running agents used GNU find syntax (-newermt '-N minutes') with stderr sent to /dev/null; on this host find rejects it, so the check reported zero writes as a RESULT when it was a silent command failure

TEST-004's watchdog-kill and interrupt sub-arms cannot be falsified by any single-point mutation because cleanup on those paths is covered twice (the in-loop iso_destroy plus the EXIT/INT/TERM traps); only two-point mutations turn them red
suites that invoke a funnel themselves pay the disposable-checkout cost again, so 9 of 81 suites exceed the 2s-per-suite bound individually (worst +20s on aai-delta-stage3) while the mean is 1.07s
TEST-001 and TEST-005(a)/(c) compare the fixture root as a STRING, so on macOS those sub-assertions can never fire
via the shared .git, one suite can arm a failing post-checkout hook that makes git worktree add fail, so every LATER suite in the run executes in the live tree
a suite in a disposable worktree can still write the shipping repository's refs, .git/config and .git/hooks, because a worktree shares one .git

the orchestrator again treated a role's 'filed:' list as proof a registry entry exists; fu-iso-suite-leaks-its-own-fixture-dirs was cited as filed in a dispatch and in a decision, and grep of decisions.jsonl returns zero
nothing COUNTS a failure to arm isolation: no counter, no summary line, no run-ledger field — all three degrade paths are a single mid-scroll log_warn
ISOLATION_BASES=() resets the array WHOLESALE at tests/skills/test-framework.sh (run_test, both the seeding-missed branch and the post-run destroy), discarding any entry it did not create
the wrapper's INT/TERM/HUP traps (.aai/scripts/aai-run-tests.sh) call aai_iso_cleanup and exit WITHOUT reaping the wrapped command's process group first
the AC Status rows must be flipped to a terminal state BEFORE close-work-item.mjs runs, not after; the orchestrator has been dispatching the opposite order

aai_iso_exec_script recognises a shell interpreter by basename only, so 'env bash tests/skills/test-framework.sh' or 'nohup bash ...' treats env/nohup as the executed script and the framework opt-out does not apply

aai-run-tests.sh isolates suite runs only, by design, so every generator, build, node one-liner and probe a role runs through the canonical wrapper executes in the shipping tree with a guard that cannot fail the run
a spec's 'Registry items closed by this scope' line is never checked against the ledger, so a frozen document can claim closures that never happened

41 of the .aai/scripts/*.mjs CLIs still print with console.log and then call process.exit, the exact shape that truncated follow-ups.mjs list --json at 65536 bytes on a pipe; docs-audit.mjs (23 logs), test-canon.mjs (28), docs-canon.mjs (23) and metrics-flush.mjs (15) are the largest payloads
follow-ups.mjs:517 has an unreachable return; after a usageError() call that can no longer return
installPipeGuard's non-EPIPE re-throw arm is read-verified only, never executed by any test
the throw-based exit contract and the EPIPE guard in follow-ups.mjs were never measured on Windows
the orchestrator ran a bite-proof mutation against the tracked suite file instead of a copy, and the first restore attempt silently failed on a mis-anchored sed pattern
TEST-021(c) never asserts its own precondition that the reader is gone before the write, so the arm reaches the same observable with the guard removed and an open reader
the orchestrator pushed a commit to main that regenerated docs/INDEX.md while a PR shipping the same generated file was open, turning that PR CONFLICTING
resolving a merge conflict in the append-only ledger by unioning both sides in the wrong order rewrites existing bytes from the base branch's point of view, even though no record is lost
allocate-doc-number.mjs TYPE_MAP has no research and no hotfix row, so --type research and --type hotfix exit 2 as unknown types
test-aai-ceremony-levels.sh TEST-016 pins .aai/scripts/lib/docs-audit-core.mjs with a bare git diff --exit-code, so ANY later scope that touches that shared library fails a test written for SPEC-0041
seven of the eight intake templates carry no number: key, so a verbatim copy now fails docs-audit --intake-file with number-absent

unescaped backticks inside a double-quoted bash string in tests/skills/lib/prompt-diet-ledger.sh ran as command substitution on every source, printing 'extra: command not found' to stderr and silently deleting the word from the ledger text

Spec-AC-02 and its AC-Status Evidence cell say every per-type prompt's OPENING directory line, but tests/skills/test-aai-intake.sh TEST-013 pins the file-wide SET of docs/<dir> mentions, which is also fence-blind and therefore brittle in the other direction

for the two intake types TYPE_MAP does not know (research, hotfix) the .aai/INTAKE_COMMON.md table row and the per-type prompt can drift together to a wrong directory with the whole intake suite green
TEST-013's no-prefix-restated loop greps for the display prefix WITH its trailing hyphen, so a hyphenless restatement such as 'the prefix for this type is CHANGE' passes

tests/skills/test-aai-intake.sh intake_table_lines requires single-space table cells while the shipped parseIntakeTypeTable in .aai/scripts/docs-audit.mjs allows \s*, so a double-spaced ninth row is live in the gate and invisible to the arm that pins row count, prefix and directory

the intake-numbers ledger entry in tests/skills/lib/prompt-diet-ledger.sh asserted 'no backtick in any ledger entry', which is literally false because line 69 carries an escaped pair; the true invariant is no UNESCAPED backtick

the shipped comment above TEST-012's anchored awk in tests/skills/test-aai-intake.sh says 'awk | grep -q would let grep's early exit SIGPIPE awk and redden the arm' as a certainty, but measured on the real prompts that pipeline returns pipestatus 0 0
the legacy FALLBACK block in .aai/INTAKE_COMMON.md still instructs scan-and-mint of docs/<type>/<TYPE>-000N-<slug>.md, which is exactly the numbered filename the new --intake-file predicate rejects

roles routinely write follow-up ids into their reports that the registry CLI refuses, because the ids exceed the hard 40-character cap, so a finding reported as filed can never have been filed under that name
test_spec0010_committed_index_idempotent strips only ^Generated: so it carries the same UTC-midnight bomb in miniature
STATE current_focus.spec_path points at the previous ride spec while ref_id is the current scope
index row metadata, headings, counts and ordering are asserted by no arm after the narrowing; the pre-commit hook is opt-in and CI has none
index_posix_findings tests every line for a backslash, not only path tokens, so a Notes cell mentioning a regex reddens the arm with index path is not POSIX
INDEX_SNAP_COMMITTED is a cp of the live docs/INDEX.md rather than git show HEAD:docs/INDEX.md, so a locally edited index is what the committed-index arm grades
index_stale_findings derives its scanned dirs from the Source: line of the index under test, so an index stale because a family was added never checks that family
TEST-004 lacks TEST-001 kept_lines guard and passes green under a total-swallow mask; the spec D4 sentence credits the raw-diff assertion instead of the guard

index_posix_findings exits 1 both for real path findings and for the predicate failing to run, and does not fold stderr into the captured output, so an infrastructure failure surfaces as a path defect with an empty message

index_strip_dated clears in_overdue only on a level-2 heading, so the Overdue mask runs to EOF if that section ever stops being followed by one, and the shipped comment claims the helper can only under-mask
